cls: KRAS G12C covalent inhibitor (RAS GTPase family inhibitor)
pharm: Oral small-molecule covalent inhibitor of KRAS G12C; traps mutant KRAS in the inactive GDP-bound state and blocks oncogenic signaling
quick: 600 mg orally twice daily, alone (NSCLC) or with cetuximab (CRC)
Can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
No adjustment in mild impairment; limited data in moderate-severe
No established adjustment; monitor; hold or reduce for hepatotoxicity
No specific interaction; limit due to GI and liver effects
ECG/QTc, electrolytes, liver tests, GI tolerance, lung symptoms
summary: Adagrasib (Krazati) is an oral KRAS G12C covalent inhibitor for adults with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, and for KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer in combination with cetuximab. The dose is 600 mg orally twice daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Key risks are GI toxicity (diarrhea, nausea, vomiting), hepatotoxicity, QTc prolongation, ILD/pneumonitis, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is a CYP3A substrate and inhibitor; avoid strong CYP3A inducers and QT-prolonging drugs where possible.
indications: Treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with KRAS G12C mutation after prior systemic therapy
Treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated colorectal cancer after prior chemotherapy, in combination with cetuximab

dosage.c: NSCLC, KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; confirm KRAS G12C mutation before starting
dosage.t: Twice daily, with or without food

dosage.c: Colorectal cancer, KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic (with cetuximab)
dosage.d: 600 mg orally twice daily, plus cetuximab per its labeling
dosage.n: For previously treated disease; continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.t: Twice daily (adagrasib); cetuximab on its own infusion schedule

dosage.d: First reduction: 400 mg twice daily; second reduction: 600 mg once daily; discontinue if not tolerated at 600 mg once daily
dosage.n: Withhold, reduce, or permanently discontinue based on severity of GI toxicity, hepatotoxicity, QTc prolongation, or ILD

admin: Take tablets by mouth twice daily, with or without food, at about the same times each day
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not chew, crush, or split
For colorectal cancer, adagrasib is given together with cetuximab IV per its own infusion protocol; confirm KRAS G12C status before starting
Obtain baseline and periodic ECGs and electrolytes; monitor liver tests and GI tolerance, and interrupt or reduce for toxicity per labeling
moa: Adagrasib is a covalent inhibitor of KRAS G12C. It binds irreversibly to the mutant cysteine residue and locks KRAS G12C in its inactive GDP-bound state, blocking downstream signaling through RAF/MEK/ERK and related pathways. This inhibits proliferation and survival of KRAS G12C-driven tumor cells in NSCLC and colorectal cancer.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to adagrasib or any excipient
monitor: ECG/QTc and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium) in patients with heart failure, bradyarrhythmias, or QT-prolonging drugs
Liver tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) for hepatotoxicity
relative: Congenital long QT syndrome or concurrent QTc prolongation
Concomitant strong CYP3A inducers or QT-prolonging drugs

preg: Based on mechanism and animal findings, adagrasib can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on adagrasib in human milk or its effects on the infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild renal impairment. Adagrasib has not been adequately studied in moderate to severe renal impairment; use with caution and monitor for GI, hepatic, and QT effects.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is established for pre-existing hepatic impairment; monitor closely. Withhold, reduce, or discontinue for treatment-emergent hepatotoxicity (Grade 2 or higher ALT/AST or bilirubin elevation) per labeling.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive GI and hepatic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ECG (QTc), electrolytes (potassium, magnesium), and liver tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin); monitor for ILD by symptoms and imaging.
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food effect described.
major: Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - reduce adagrasib exposure; avoid
QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., certain antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, fluoroquinolones, macrolides) - additive QTc risk; avoid or monitor ECG closely
Sensitive CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic index (e.g., tacrolimus, cyclosporine) - adagrasib inhibits CYP3A and raises their levels; avoid or monitor closely
minor: Gastric acid-reducing agents - no major effect described for adagrasib absorption
moderate: Strong CYP3A inhibitors - increase adagrasib exposure; monitor for toxicity
CYP2D6 and P-gp substrates (adagrasib inhibits CYP2D6 and P-gp) - may raise levels of substrates such as dextromethorphan or digoxin; monitor
Drugs that lower potassium or magnesium (e.g., diuretics) - worsen QT risk; correct electrolytes

emergency: Syncope, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation/arrhythmia)
New or worsening cough, dyspnea, or fever (pneumonitis)
Severe or bloody diarrhea with dehydration
Jaundice, dark urine, or severe abdominal pain (liver injury)

monitoring: ECG and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium) at baseline, during treatment, and with QT-prolonging co-meds or cardiac risk factors
Liver tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) at baseline and periodically; evaluate promptly for hepatotoxicity
GI tolerance (diarrhea, nausea, vomiting), hydration status, and electrolytes
Pulmonary symptoms; withhold and evaluate for ILD/pneumonitis and discontinue if confirmed
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Take 600 mg twice daily with or without food; swallow tablets whole and do not make up a missed dose by doubling
Report severe diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, or fatigue, and stay hydrated
Report yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, right-sided abdominal pain, or unusual bleeding (liver injury)
Seek care for fainting, palpitations, new cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, or fever (heart rhythm or lung effects)
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose; do not breastfeed; tell your team about all other medicines, especially heart-rhythm drugs
pk: Target inhibition with first doses; tumor responses develop over weeks
Median Tmax about 6 hours after oral dosing
Steady state within about 8 days of twice-daily dosing
pearls: Confirm KRAS G12C mutation with an FDA-approved test before starting; for colorectal cancer, give only with cetuximab
Standard dose is 600 mg twice daily, higher pill burden than most TKIs; counsel on adherence and GI tolerance
QTc prolongation: avoid in congenital long QT or concurrent QTc prolongation, correct electrolytes, and monitor ECGs
Hepatotoxicity is common; dose interruption and reduction rules are driven by ALT/AST and bilirubin grades
GI toxicity (diarrhea, nausea, vomiting) is the most frequent reason for interruption; manage early with antiemetics and hydration
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once to make up a missed dose. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next dose at the regular time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for adagrasib overdose. Manage with supportive care, including ECG and electrolyte monitoring for QT effects, liver tests, antiemetics and fluids for GI toxicity, and observation for ILD symptoms. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
